title: "Guided Project: Statistical Transformations and Coordinate Systems"
subtitle: "CIS-3901 · Module 12"

## Purpose

In Module 12 you learned that ggplot2 computes before it draws (stats), and
that the frame a plot is drawn in can change what a reader sees
(coordinates). In this Guided Project you use both on **your own** Fairness
and Sports data, and you publish your findings as a **Quarto report** on your
own website, the one you set up in Module 10.

You'll practice turning counts into rates (and choosing the total you divide
by), showing a summary with its n and its spread, deciding between zooming
and filtering, and choosing the frame (sideways bars). These are the moves your
Challenge Project reports will need.

## What you'll hand in

1. Your **published report** (a web page on your GitHub Pages site), showing
   your code and its output.
2. In Blackboard: the link to your report (step 6).
3. AI disclosure: AI use line in your report, AI log typed in Blackboard (or the
   no-AI statement), and copies of all AI conversations uploaded in Blackboard
   (step 6).

## Words you'll use

- **Share:** a part ÷ a total. It has no unit. Always say *of what*.
- **Rate:** a share of a group that has an outcome: outcome count ÷ group
  size (e.g., a school's graduation rate). This is **question A**.
- **Question B:** of everyone with the outcome, what share is each group?
  Same counts, a different total.
- **sd** = spread of the individuals; **se** = spread of the mean (or rate):
  how much it would move with another sample of the same size.
- **Lie Factor** (Tufte, 2001, p. 57): how many times a picture exaggerates a
  difference.

## Steps

All steps happen in your **`cis-3901-projects`** project in Posit Cloud
(course space CIS-3901-Fall2026), not in a new assignment. Keep this page open
while you work.

### Step 0 · One-time setting (1 minute)

**Tools → Project Options → General:** set *Restore .RData into workspace at
startup* to **No** and *Save workspace to .RData on exit* to **Never**. Then
**Session → Restart R**. (This stops old objects from coming back and hiding
errors.)

### Step 1 · Bring your two data files (5 minutes)

Your verified Fairness file (`fairness.csv`) and your Sports file
(`sports.csv`) are in the `data/` folder of your Module 11 Guided Project,
**`guided_project_aes_geoms`**.

1. Open `guided_project_aes_geoms`. In the Files pane, open `data/`, tick
   **only** `fairness.csv` → **More → Export → Download**. Do the same for
   `sports.csv`. (One file at a time: ticking both downloads a zip.)
2. Open `cis-3901-projects`. In the Files pane:
   - go to `data/tidy/` → **Upload** → `fairness.csv`;
   - go to `data/sports/` → **Upload** → `sports.csv`.

Names matter: exactly `data/tidy/fairness.csv` and `data/sports/sports.csv`.
If your browser renamed a download (for example `fairness (1).csv`), rename
it in the Files pane (tick it → **Rename**). If you upload a file to the top
folder or to `data/` by mistake, the script moves it to the right place and
tells you.

**Your data files are published with your report.** You push them to your
public repository in step 5, so anyone can see them, as with your report.

**Privacy:** private people's names must not be in your files or in your
plots (for example, runners' names in the Boston Marathon data). Professional
athletes, teams and officials are public figures and are fine.

### Step 2 · Add the starter files (2 minutes)

Download **`gp12_starter.zip`** from Blackboard. In
`cis-3901-projects`, go to the **top folder** (`project`) → **Upload** →
the zip. Posit Cloud unzips it and adds:

```default
scripts/gp12_stats_coords.R    the code: run it task by task
reports/gp12_report.qmd        your report: write your findings here
```

### Step 3 · Work through the script (most of your time)

Open `scripts/gp12_stats_coords.R`. Run **Section 0** first. Then, task by task:

- **Read** the code and the comments. **Predict** what the plot will show
  (write your prediction in the report).
- **Change** the lines marked **YOUR TURN**, run the task, and read the
  check: `PASS: A1` or `TO DO: A1: …` with what to fix.

| Task | Fairness (Part A) | Sports (Part B) | From class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Your group and outcome | Group, outcome and a numeric value | Session 1, slide 17 |
| 1 | Rate within each group (question A) | Same, you write the plot | Session 1, slides 10, 17 |
| 2 | Rates with their se | Mean with sd and se | Session 1, slides 13–16 |
| 3 | Zoom or filter? Lie Factor | Same, you write the plots | Session 2, slides 4–7 |
| 4 | Each group's share of everyone with the outcome (question B) | Same | Session 1, slide 17; Session 2, slide 9 |

Part A has more help; Part B asks you to write more of the code yourself,
using Part A as your model.

### Step 4 · Write your report

Open `reports/gp12_report.qmd`. It already runs your script and shows your
plots. Replace every **WRITE:** line with your own sentences, replace each
`fig-alt` with one sentence about **your** plot, and put your name (a first
name or initials is fine) as the author.

Your rendered report will look like the [practice page](practice.html):
your code in grey boxes, with its output under it.

### Step 5 · Render, commit, push (5 minutes)

1. Click **Render** on `gp12_report.qmd`. Check the page: your plots, your
   writing, and the **Checks** table at the end.
2. **Git** tab → tick every file listed, including `data/tidy/fairness.csv`
   and `data/sports/sports.csv` → **Commit** (message: "Guided Project 12") → **Push** (your token, as in
   Module 10).
3. After a minute or two, open
   `https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/cis-3901-projects/reports/gp12_report.html`.

You can render and push as often as you like; the last push before the due
date is the one that counts.

### Step 6 · Submit in Blackboard

In the Blackboard assignment for this Guided Project:

1. **Type in the text box** the link to your report, your AI log and the
   attestation. Copy this template:

   ```default
   Report: https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/cis-3901-projects/reports/gp12_report.html

   AI log
   Use 1 – Tool: ___ | What I used it for: ___ | What I changed or checked, and why: ___
   Use 2 – Tool: ___ | What I used it for: ___ | What I changed or checked, and why: ___
   (add a line per use; upload a copy of every conversation)

   OR: I did not use AI for this project. How I worked through problems: ___

   Attestation: This log lists every use of AI in this project.
   ```

2. **Upload copies of all your AI conversations** as .txt, PDF or Word, saved
   on your own computer, with personal information removed. **Never put the log
   or the conversations in your Posit Cloud project:** everything there is
   pushed to the public site. Blackboard doesn't accept `.html`.
3. **If pushing failed** (token, Pages not updating): zip
   `docs/reports/gp12_report.html` (one file, plots included), attach the zip,
   and say what went wrong. A technical problem won't cost you the grade.

## Success criteria

- Section 0 runs; your report renders; the Checks table shows **PASS** for the
  tasks you did. Aim for all ten.
- Each plot has a one-sentence `fig-alt` that describes **your** plot.
- Your writing answers each **WRITE:** prompt in your own words, with numbers
  from your plots (rates, n, Lie Factor).
- For tasks 1 and 4 you say which question (A or B) your Module 11 question
  needs, and why.
- Small groups are shown, with their n, not dropped: under-represented is not
  unimportant.
- The page is published, the link works, your two data files are in your
  repository, and no private person's name appears anywhere.

## Ideas for your columns (check them with `glimpse()`)

Use these as starting points; check them with `glimpse()` in your own file.
Every class dataset gets the same kind of hint. Small groups stay in your
plots, with their n.

**Fairness**

- **Adult:** group `sex` or `race`; outcome `income == ">50K"`.
- **ACS Income:** group `sex` or `str_trunc(race, 30)` (the full race labels
  are too long for a plot, and some groups are very small: one has n = 1, so
  `a3_start` must be below 1); outcome `income > 50000`.
- **Diabetes Hospital:** group `race` or `age` (three bands); outcome
  `readmit_30_days == 1`.
- **Credit Card** (`fairness.csv` = your clients file): group `sex` or
  `education` (one group has n = 2); outcome `default_next_month == "yes"`.

**Sports**

- **NFL Draft Combine:** group `position`; outcome `Round %in% 1` (picked in
  round 1; `Round` is empty for players not drafted, and `%in%` counts them
  as FALSE); value `forty`.
- **WNBA game statistics:** group `team_home_away`; outcome `team_winner`.
  The file has no score column, so use the days since the team's previous
  game as the value: start with `sports %>% arrange(game_date) %>%
  group_by(team_id, season) %>% mutate(...)`, with
  `value = as.numeric(game_date - lag(game_date))` inside `mutate()`, then
  add `%>% ungroup()`. Home and away have the same count, so B3's Lie Factor
  is 1.
- **Setka Cup table tennis:** group sets played,
  `factor(Sets_P1 + Sets_P2)` (3, 4 or 5; `factor()` makes them groups, not
  a number line); outcome `HomeWinner == 1`; value points in game 1,
  `P1_G1 + P2_G1`.
- **Sumo:** group the rank's first letter, `str_sub(Rank, 1, 1)`; outcome
  `wins > losses`; value `weight_kg` or `height_cm`.
- **WTA Grand Slam matches:** group `surface` or `round`; outcome
  `minutes > 120` (or a threshold you choose); value `minutes`. Some matches
  have no `minutes`: they show as NA in the legend of A1-style plots.
- **MMA fight decisions:** group `factor(rounds)` (3, 5 or 12); outcome
  `agreement == "Agree"` (all three judges agree); value
  `abs(judge1_margin)`. (Not `result_type`: Unanimous almost always means
  Agree, so its rates are close to 0% or 100%.)
- **MLB pitches:** group `player_name` or `pitch_type` (includes NA and
  types with n = 2 or 5: they stay, with their n); outcome `result == "S"`
  (a strike); value `release_speed`.
